Header:
Date: 2026-07-05
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Ellen Rivers (Redwood CSM), Tom Bauer (CTO, Seamist), Priya Nair (Lead ML Eng), Derek Olsen (Head Ops), Rosa Kim (Security Architect)

Optional auto sections (may have errors):
Summary: Align pilot and infra intake; decision point is pilot success metrics and whether Dedicated or Private required.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, I'm the AE on this. Quick round of intros?
[00:12] Tom Bauer: Hey all, Tom here, CTO at Seamist. We're excited, we run a recommender + support assistant combo, lots of real-time inference.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Priya, Lead ML eng, I own the model infra.
[00:22] Derek Olsen: Derek, ops, I handle networking and infra provisioning.
[00:26] Rosa Kim: Rosa, security. I'll be looking at KMS, audit logs, and our SSO.
[00:32] Maya Chen: Great — Arjun from Redwood will walk through the technical footprint and runbook items; Ellen will be your CSM for onboarding cadence. Arjun?
[00:40] Arjun Patel: Hi all. Quick agenda: understand current stack, latency/cost goals, constraints around data residency/encryption, then map to pilot options: Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). Then next steps and a short benchmark plan.
[00:58] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Quick context: we have a mixture of user-facing assistant calls (median prompt length small, tail to 6k tokens), plus background batch embeddings for search. We host on GCP, using k8s for app tier and a mix of CPU and some GPU for training. We haven't fully committed to any inference vendor; we've been doing an in-house prototype with optimized quantized Llama variants.
[01:25] Maya Chen: Ok. So you're hybrid workload — low-latency interactive and higher-throughput embedding batch. Typical split?
[01:30] Priya Nair: Roughly 70% interactive, 30% batch but batch runs weekly spikes. Peak concurrency around 350 rps for assistant path during campaign windows.
[01:45] Arjun Patel: Good to know. On Redwood side we can route by policy so interactive goes to low-latency pool (Dedicated) and batch to cheaper quantized variants. We also do prefix/KV caching to reduce token cost for similar prompts. Note: transcription might say KV "cash" in some exports, but I promise it's cache.
[02:05] Derek Olsen: For Dedicated, what's the network footprint? We need VPC peering or private link, we can't open public endpoints in prod for now.
[02:12] Arjun Patel: For Dedicated you can either use provisioned private peering (we support VPC peering in most regions) or Redwood Private which gives you an air-gapped control plane option. Network egress patterns depend on model placement; if you put Dedicated in customer's project, egress is internal.
[02:28] Rosa Kim: Security questions up front: do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), audit logs retention, and SAML SSO? Also SOC 2 is a must.
[02:37] Ellen Rivers: Yes — at a high level Redwood supports CMK via KMS integrations, we have audit log exports and can increase retention with an add-on, and SAML SSO/SCIM for user provisioning. Our hosted environment is SOC 2 compliant; Private deployments can meet stricter controls. We'll share the security pack after the call.
[02:53] Tom Bauer: Great. Pricing will matter — if Dedicated is required for security, what's the uplift vs hosted?
[02:59] Maya Chen: We'll put tiered pricing in the SOW: hosted per-token, Dedicated commit models monthly, and Private as enterprise license. We'll include sample math for your workload.
[03:10] Priya Nair: For benchmarking — we want 95th percentile latency under 300ms for interactive path at 350 rps. Is that realistic?
[03:18] Arjun Patel: Yes, with a right model slice and GPU types you can hit that. A few gotchas: sequence lengths and KV cache hit-rate will greatly impact latency. We'll need sample prompt sets to simulate tail latency.
[03:30] Derek Olsen: Also cold-starts — we need warm pools or fast spin-up. What does Redwood do for that?
[03:36] Arjun Patel: We support warm replicas and pre-warming policies; Dedicated supports faster scale by preallocating GPU-backed slots. We can also set fallback policies to lighter models if capacity is constrained.
[03:48] Rosa Kim: About data residency — some EU customers mean we need to ensure data never leaves region. Can Redwood pin models to region?
[03:55] Maya Chen: Yes, routing policies can pin by region. For Private we can run fully in your VPC in-region.
[04:02] Tom Bauer: Good. Let's talk pilot scope. We want to validate cost/perf for assistant path and verify security posture. Thinking 3-week pilot: week 1 ingest prompts & run small bench, week 2 scale scenario, week 3 production-ish smoke tests. Thoughts?
[04:14] Arjun Patel: That aligns. We'll provide a runbook: infra diagram, test harness, and expected metrics (latency p95, error rate, tokens/unit cost). For the bench we'll need sample traffic shape and prompt sets.
[04:26] Priya Nair: We'll also need request tracing — can Redwood integrate with our tracing? We use OpenTelemetry.
[04:32] Arjun Patel: We have tracing hooks and per-request metadata; we can emit traces to your collector in Dedicated/Private setups. For hosted we can surface trace links in Redwood Console but exporting raw spans is limited unless in Private.
[04:46] Derek Olsen: On the network side, we have strict egress rules: only certain destinations allowed. How do you recommend connecting?
[04:52] Ellen Rivers: We typically recommend VPC peering for Dedicated or Private for full control. We'll map your egress policy in the network intake doc.
[05:00] Tom Bauer: Are there known gotchas with quantization? Priya is worried about regressions in quality.
[05:06] Arjun Patel: Quantization reduces model size and cost but can affect quality depending on prompt sensitivity. Redwood Optimize gives suggested quantization profiles per workload and we run evals tied to your prompt set to detect regressions. The pilot includes a quality regression check.
[05:20] Priya Nair: Good. We will send two golden prompt suites and an edge-case set.
[05:25] Maya Chen: Great. I'll log that as an action.
[05:28] [00:05:40] brief cross talk / audio drop (speaker overlap)
[05:50] Priya Nair: Another thing — we use embeddings for semantic search, cost is a concern. Can batching help?
[05:56] Arjun Patel: Yes. For embeddings, batching and async pipelines are the main levers. We can show batch size vs latency/cost curves. If you can accept slightly higher tail latency for embeddings, cost drops significantly.
[06:10] Tom Bauer: On governance, how granular is RBAC? We need per-team token restrictions.
[06:15] Ellen Rivers: RBAC and token scoping are supported; we can restrict routes and set quotas per team. We'll include a sample RBAC policy.
[06:24] Rosa Kim: Pen-test and vulnerability scanning cadence? We need recent reports for vendor risk.
[06:29] Maya Chen: We will attach our latest SOC 2 report, penetration test summary, and vulnerability management policies in the security pack.
[06:38] Derek Olsen: Ok, let's get into some technical specifics — Arjun can you sketch expected GPU types and ops for our profile?
[06:44] Arjun Patel: Sure — for low-latency interactive at that scale, A10/H100 class with optimized kernels, plus sharded KV for long-context workloads. For cost-sensitive batch, 8-bit quantized variants on T4-class might be fine. Our runtime picks kernels based on sequence length distribution — note sometimes docs say kernel "sellection" in the transcriptions, you'll see typos.
[07:05] Priya Nair: We need to be explicit about memory and sequence lengths; some of our prompts go to 6k tokens which affects GPU memory and throughput.
[07:12] Arjun Patel: We'll run a sizing exercise in the runbook. Also prefix caching can cut repeated prompt costs if you have many similar contexts.
[07:21] Maya Chen: For the pilot, do you prefer we spin up a sandbox Dedicated environment or use hosted with Private network peering?
[07:29] Tom Bauer: My security team leans towards Dedicated in our project or Private, not public hosted. Rosa?
[07:33] Rosa Kim: Prefer Dedicated with VPC peering initially, see if audit logs and KMS integration suffice; if we need stricter controls we'll evaluate a Private deployment.
[07:42] Maya Chen: Ok we'll default pilot to Dedicated with VPC peering. We'll include a path for Private if needed.
[07:47] [00:08:00] short pause, background noise
[07:58] Derek Olsen: On implementation: who will own infra changes? We prefer Redwood provide terraform modules or a runbook.
[08:04] Arjun Patel: We'll provide terraform modules where appropriate and an infra-as-code example for peering and security groups.
[08:11] Priya Nair: About observability — per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown would be critical.
[08:17] Ellen Rivers: Redwood Console has per-model/per-route dashboards and we can export logs to your SIEM. We'll include retention options.
[08:25] Tom Bauer: Great. Let's talk timelines — we want pilot running mid-July and decision by end of July. Doable?
[08:31] Maya Chen: Yes; timeline: runbook + pricing by next week, infra setup in the following week, bench test week of July 13, then smoke to prod by end-of-month for decision.
[08:40] Priya Nair: That works if we get runbook and example configs promptly.
[08:44] Maya Chen: Actionable items we'll put in CRM, but quick recap now.
[08:49] Arjun Patel: I'll attach runbook + example terraform + sample batch configs. Also I'll include guidance on batch sizing and caching parameters.
[08:56] Rosa Kim: I'll send the security questionnaire and KMS spec.
[08:59] Priya Nair: I'll drop two prompt suites and a small traffic shape CSV.
[09:04] Derek Olsen: I'll coordinate with our network team for peering windows.
[09:09] Maya Chen: Next steps: Maya to send pilot SOW and pricing (includes hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options), Arjun sends runbook and infra bits, Rosa and Priya provide docs. Then schedule bench test for week of July 13. Any other questions?
[09:22] Tom Bauer: No, thanks all.
[09:24] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the attachments.
[09:27] -- End --
